slides.title: Introduction to OOP
content: Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) is a programming paradigm based on objects containing data and methods
Objects represent real-world entities with attributes (data) and behaviors (methods)
It improves code organization, reusability, and scalability
It is widely used in modern programming languages like Java

slides.title: Why OOP is Used
content: Procedural programming is difficult to manage for large applications
OOP organizes code into objects, making it modular and maintainable
It supports reusability using inheritance and flexibility using polymorphism
It models real-world systems effectively

slides.title: OOP vs Procedural Programming
content: Procedural programming follows step-by-step execution, OOP focuses on objects
Data is globally accessible in procedural but encapsulated in OOP
OOP provides better security and modularity
OOP is more scalable for large systems

slides.title: Class in OOP
content: A class is a blueprint or template for creating objects
It defines attributes (data) and methods (functions)
It does not occupy memory until objects are created
Example: Employee class with name and salary

slides.title: Object in OOP
content: An object is an instance of a class
It represents a real-world entity with its own data
Objects occupy memory and interact using methods
Each object has separate memory even if from same class

slides.title: Attributes (Fields)
content: Attributes are variables that store data of an object
They represent the state of the object
Example: name and balance in BankAccount
They are usually declared private for data security

slides.title: Methods (Functions)
content: Methods define the behavior of an object
They perform operations using attributes
Example: deposit(), withdraw(), getBalance()
They provide controlled access to object data

slides.title: Encapsulation Concept
content: Encapsulation means wrapping data and methods into a single unit
Attributes are kept private to restrict direct access
Access is provided using public methods
It ensures data security and integrity

slides.title: Getters and Setters
content: Getters are methods used to retrieve attribute values
Setters are methods used to update attribute values
They provide controlled access to private data
Example: getBalance(), setName()

slides.title: Interaction of Attributes and Methods
content: Methods operate on attributes to perform actions
Private attributes cannot be accessed directly outside class
Methods act as an interface between user and data
Ensures controlled modification of object state

slides.title: BankAccount Example
content: Attributes: name (String), balance (double)
Methods: deposit(), withdraw(), getBalance()
Balance is private to protect user data
Methods ensure safe operations like checking balance before withdrawal

slides.title: Important OOP Practices
content: Always use getters and setters for private attributes
Validate inputs inside methods to prevent errors
Keep sensitive data private for security
Use methods to maintain data integrity

slides.title: Java as OOP Language
content: Java is a class-based, object-oriented programming language
Everything in Java is built around classes and objects
It supports OOP features like encapsulation and inheritance
Programs start from the main method inside a class

slides.title: Basic Structure of Java Program
content: Java programs are written inside classes
Execution starts from main() method
System.out.println is used to print output
Java follows 'Write Once, Run Anywhere' concept

slides.title: Constructor in Java
content: A constructor is a special method called when an object is created
It initializes object attributes
Constructor name must match class name
It does not have a return type

slides.title: Types of Constructors
content: Non-parameterized constructor: no arguments
Parameterized constructor: initializes with given values
Copy constructor: copies values from another object
Constructors can be overloaded with different parameters

slides.title: Default Constructor Behavior
content: If no constructor is defined, Java creates a default constructor
Primitive types get default values like 0
Reference types like String get null
Local variables are not automatically initialized

slides.title: Constructor Overloading
content: Multiple constructors with different parameters in same class
Allows flexible object initialization
Improves code readability and reuse
Example: Employee(), Employee(name), Employee(name, salary)

slides.title: Constructor Chaining
content: One constructor calls another using this()
Helps avoid duplicate code
this() must be first statement in constructor
Improves maintainability and consistency

slides.title: Memory in Java (Stack vs Heap)
content: Objects are stored in heap memory
References and primitive variables are stored in stack
Heap memory is managed by Garbage Collector
Stack memory is cleared after method execution

slides.title: Object Creation and Deletion
content: Objects are created using new keyword
Memory is allocated in heap
Objects are deleted automatically by Garbage Collector
Setting reference to null makes object eligible for deletion

slides.title: Advantages of OOP
content: Code reusability using inheritance
Better security using encapsulation
Flexibility using polymorphism
Scalable and maintainable for large applications
